title: Resilient LLM API Client
summary: Build a client that retries transient failures with backoff and jitter, falls back to a secondary model on persistent failure, and fails fast on non-retryable errors.
requirements: Classify errors as retryable or non-retryable based on a status code or explicit flag.
Implement exponential backoff with full jitter, with a configurable base delay and cap.
Retry only retryable failures, up to a fixed maximum.
Fall back to a secondary function exactly once after the primary is exhausted or blocked.
start: Start from Module 6's exercise function and wire real (or realistically mocked) delay timing using an injected sleep function, so your tests can run fast with a fake clock instead of actually waiting.
acceptance: A primary call that succeeds immediately never touches the fallback.
A retryable failure is retried up to the configured max, with delay growing per the full-jitter formula.
A non-retryable failure stops retrying immediately, regardless of how high the max retry count is set.
Exhausting retries on the primary triggers exactly one fallback attempt, not a second full retry cycle.
Both primary and fallback failing returns a clear structured failure, never an uncaught rejection.
tests: Primary succeeds on the first call → fallback never invoked.
Primary fails twice (retryable) then succeeds → primary invoked 3 times, fallback never invoked.
Primary fails once with a non-retryable error, max_retries=5 → primary invoked exactly once, fallback invoked once.
Primary always fails (retryable), max_retries=2 → primary invoked 3 times, fallback invoked exactly once.
Both primary and fallback fail → function returns normally (doesn't raise) with a structured failure object.
mistakes: Checking the retry count before checking retryability, wasting the whole budget on a guaranteed-permanent failure.
Giving fallback the same retry budget as the primary instead of a single bounded attempt.
Using a real asyncio.sleep() in tests instead of an injected fake, making the suite slow.
solution: Loop: `await` primary, on success return immediately.
On exception, check `getattr(e, 'retryable', True) is not False`; if non-retryable or out of retries, break to fallback.
Otherwise increment attempt and retry (with a jittered delay in a real system, injected/mocked in tests).
After the loop, try fallback exactly once, returning its result or a structured failure.
